1 غَطَسَهُ , (S, A, K,) aor.
غَطِسَ , (S, TA,) inf. n. غَطْسٌ; (S;) or ↓ غطّسهُ , (Msb,) inf. n. تَغْطِيسٌ; (TA;) or both: (A. TA;) He immersed, immerged, dipped, plunged, or sunk, him or it, in water. (S, A, Msb * K, TA.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] ↓ غَطَّسَنِى فِى بَحْرِ ٱنْعُمِهِ He overwhelmed me in the sea of his benefits, or favours]. (A.) ＝
-A2- غَطَسَ, aor.
غَطِسَ , (Msb, K,) inf. n. غَطْسٌ, (Msb,) He, or it, became immersed, immerged, dipped, plunged, or sunk, in water or he immersed, or immerged himself, plunged, or dived, in water (Msb, * K) ―
-b2- غَطَسَ فِى الإِنَآءِ He put his mouth into the vessel and so drank. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ＝
-A3- غَطَسَتْ بِهِ اللُّجَمُ Death took him away: (Sgh, K:) a dial. var. of عَطَسَتْ [q. v.]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
